statement: Global Hunger increases by 0.01 per second and is clamped to 0..100.
Hunger enters warning above 80 and dying above 99.9.
While Hunger is dying, Player Health is reduced by 0.1 per second.
Global Thirst increases by 0.02 per second and is clamped to 0..100.
Thirst warns above 80; above 99.9 the dying state reduces Health by 0.1 per second.
Global Fatigue increases by 0.02 per second and is clamped to 0..100.
At >99.9 Fatigue, the FSM sets PlayerCamera/UseBed.SleepTime to 6 and sends Activate to Player/Sleep.
The global variable named Sanity behaves as an adverse load; its base FSM subtracts 0.05 per second toward zero.
Sanity display begins above 20, warning/effects above 80, mutant spawning above 90, and dying above 95.
In the Sanity dying state, Player Health is reduced by 0.35 per second.
Above Sanity 90, SanityMutantSpawn waits 8..15 seconds and spawns a selected EnemySpawn entry around the player with X/Z offsets -25..25 and Y +5.
Sleep activation applies Fatigue -100, Drunkenness -100, Sanity -30, Hunger +10, Thirst +15, Health +40, and disables weed/alcohol effects.
Player Health is clamped to 0..100; playerDeath fires when Health falls below approximately 0.4.
FallDamage checks GroundTest.fallingTime; after more than 2 seconds it multiplies fallingTime by -9 and routes the value into body-part damage.
Player/InCar tracks InCarInt/InCarBool and switches movement, headbob, footsteps and damage-effect behavior between OnFoot and InCar states.
PlayerCamera/UseFood ray-picks item-related objects within 2 units and reacts to Use input.
SaveLoadGame coordinates save/load, references SaveGame1.es3, world seed, timeline and MapMagic position, and broadcasts save/load-related events.
At +0.01/s, Hunger reaches 100 from 0 in about 166.7 real-time minutes if unmodified.
At +0.02/s, Thirst reaches 100 from 0 in about 83.3 real-time minutes if unmodified.
At +0.02/s, Fatigue reaches 100 from 0 in about 83.3 real-time minutes if unmodified.

title: Floating origin
statement: The game uses NWH.Common.FloatingOrigin on the Player, with a distance threshold of 1,000 meters.

title: Origin shifting
statement: When the camera moves 1,000 meters from the origin, the game shifts all scene-root objects by the negative camera position during LateUpdate.

title: Coordinate instability
statement: Absolute Unity world coordinates are not stable across floating-origin shifts. The MapMagic root can serve as a stable reference anchor for relative coordinates.

title: Object deactivation
statement: __GameManager__ runs DeactivateFarAwayItems approximately every 5 seconds, deactivating eligible objects more than 1,000 meters from the Player.

title: Object destruction
statement: DeleteFarAwayItems runs approximately every 10 seconds, destroying eligible objects beyond 5,000 meters, including their children.

title: Vehicle distance behavior
statement: Cars are exempt from distance-based deactivation but become kinematic beyond 2,000 meters through DistanceKinematic.

title: Distance reference
statement: These distance-based systems calculate distance from the Player, not necessarily the active camera.

title: Object registries
statement: The game uses NewGO_ArrayList proxies, including ArrayList_Items, ArrayList_Cars, and ArrayList_Sandstorms, to manage registered objects.

title: Registration determines persistence
statement: Only registered objects participate in the game's corresponding save and distance-culling systems.

title: Object naming convention
statement: Newly created objects use names resembling <prefab>(Clone)N, with itemNameID providing a numerical identifier.

title: Object initialization
statement: Certain spawned objects support initialization through a Randomize event.

title: Inactive objects and saving
statement: Inactive GameObjects do not receive the game's SaveGame event.

title: ES3 component serialization
statement: The game's ES3 serialization can attempt to save components attached to persistent GameObjects, including runtime-added components.

title: Vehicle-child persistence
statement: Runtime-added children of vehicles are not automatically persisted.

title: Staggered loading
statement: Saved NPCs, items, points of interest, and equipped backpacks may reappear progressively over several seconds after loading.

title: Save framework
statement: The game uses Easy Save 3 (ES3) with caching.

title: Save cache behavior
statement: Save operations write through an ES3 cache, which is eventually flushed to disk. External file changes made before the flush can be overwritten.

title: Active save path
statement: ES3Settings.defaultSettings.path identifies the active save slot during normal gameplay.

title: Load transitions
statement: The active save path may be empty or stale while a save is loading.

title: PlayMaker save variables
statement: FSM variables such as SaveFile may not accurately reflect the current save slot.

title: Save-state transition
statement: The SaveLoadGame FSM returns to an isPlay state after the save sequence.

title: Serialization phase
statement: The Save_NewGO_ArrayList FSM includes a state named store cached file.

title: PlayMaker architecture
statement: The game relies extensively on PlayMaker finite-state machines for gameplay logic and interactions.

title: FSM restart behavior
statement: PlayMaker FSMs normally restart when their GameObject is re-enabled because Fsm.RestartOnEnable defaults to true.

title: Third-person vehicle camera
statement: Switching to the third-person car camera disables the entire PlayerCamera hierarchy, potentially restarting FSMs underneath it when re-enabled.

title: Vehicle attachment initialization
statement: Certain vehicle-part FSMs start in a CheckTag state that detaches the object from its parent and adds a Rigidbody.

title: Pause behavior
statement: PlayMaker FSMs continue running when Time.timeScale is zero. Some input-processing actions can therefore execute while the pause menu is open.

title: Legacy input system
statement: Gameplay actions use Unity's legacy Input Manager, commonly through PlayMaker GetButtonDown actions.

title: Named input actions
statement: Input axes/buttons include Use, Weapon 1/2/3, Weapon off, Drop Weapon, Reload, Jump, Horn, Use Bandage, Use First Aid, Rotate Item, Change Camera, and Adjust-*.

title: Built-in shortcuts
statement: F2 triggers Heal, F9 hides the UI, and F11 enables God mode.

title: God mode behavior
statement: The F11 mode provides noclip and invisibility, but does not grant invulnerability.

title: Physics query defaults
statement: The project has Physics.queriesHitTriggers = true and Physics.queriesHitBackfaces = true.

title: Trigger collision queries
statement: Raycasts can hit trigger colliders, including NPC head triggers.

title: NPC head-hit behavior
statement: NPC head triggers are associated with a 2× damage multiplier.

title: Rigidbody collision-query behavior
statement: Setting Rigidbody.detectCollisions = false can make an object undetectable to raycasts.

title: Persisted Rigidbody state
statement: ES3 persists the detectCollisions property on saved objects.

title: Non-convex MeshCollider limitations
statement: Collider.ClosestPoint on non-convex mesh colliders may return the supplied input point rather than a useful surface point.

title: TerrainCollider limitations
statement: Similar closest-point limitations can affect terrain colliders.

title: Overlap-query limitations
statement: Mesh and terrain overlap queries may detect triangle intersections without recognizing that a point or volume is entirely enclosed by geometry.

title: Raycast hit enumeration
statement: Physics.RaycastAll and RaycastNonAlloc provide a single hit per collider in the observed game environment, rather than every triangle intersection.

title: Sweep-query limitations
statement: Physics sweep queries may ignore colliders already overlapping the swept object's starting position.

title: No prebuilt NavMesh
statement: The game does not use a baked Unity NavMesh for its vanilla NPC navigation.

title: Vanilla NPC navigation
statement: NPC chase behavior relies on random-walk movement and raycast-based obstacle detection.

title: Navigation-related assembly
statement: AIModule is included with the game, potentially allowing runtime use of Unity's navigation functionality.

title: Player hierarchy changes in vehicles
statement: When driving, the Player becomes a child of a hierarchy resembling <car>/DriveTrigger/sitPos/Player.

title: NPC hierarchy changes in vehicles
statement: Seated NPCs can become descendants of a vehicle, meaning their transform.root points to the car instead of the NPC.

title: NPC identity
statement: NPC hierarchies can be identified by a Health PlayMaker FSM.

title: Vehicle identity
statement: Objects named or marked vehPart and components such as VehicleController can identify vehicle-related hierarchy boundaries.

title: Scene transitions
statement: The game destroys ordinary plugin-created GameObjects during scene loading unless they have appropriate persistence handling.

title: Game-managed object state
statement: Vanilla systems may leave temporary modifications on objects, expecting corresponding release or cleanup logic to restore their original behavior.
